message.content:
**Famous American composers (across genres and eras)**  

| Composer | Era / Genre | Notable works / contributions |
|----------|-------------|--------------------------------|
| **John Williams** | 20th–21st century, film | *Star Wars*, *Indiana Jones*, *Jurassic Park*, *Harry Potter* (first two films) |
| **Leonard Bernstein** | 20th century, classical & Broadway | *West Side Story*, *Candide*, *On the Town*; conductor of New York Philharmonic |
| **Aaron Copland** | 20th century, classical | *Appalachian Spring*, *Rodeo*, *Fanfare for the Common Man* |
| **George Gershwin** | Early–mid‑20th century, popular & classical | *Rhapsody in Blue*, *Porgy and Bess*, *An American in Paris* |
| **Philip Glass** | Late 20th–21st century, minimalism | *Einstein on the Beach*, *Glassworks*, *Koyaanisqatsi* (score) |
| **Steve Reich** | Late 20th–21st century, minimalism | *Music for 18 Musicians*, *Different Trains*, *Electric Counterpoint* |
| **John Adams** | Late 20th–21st century, contemporary classical | *Nixon in China*, *Short Ride in a Fast Machine*, *Shaker Loops* |
| **William Grant Still** | 20th century, classical | *Afro-American Symphony*, *Bluebird*, *The Spirit of the Black Hills* |
| **Samuel Barber** | 20th century, classical | *Adagio for Strings*, *Knoxville: Summer of 1915*, *Violin Concerto* |
| **Charles Ives** | Early–mid‑20th century, experimental | *The Unanswered Question*, *Concord Sonata*, *The Unanswered Question* |
| **George Gershwin** | Early–mid‑20th century, popular & classical | *Rhapsody in Blue*, *Porgy and Bess*, *An American in Paris* |
| **John Philip Sousa** | Late 19th–early 20th century, marches | “The Stars and Stripes Forever,” “The Liberty Bell” |
| **Duke Ellington** | 20th century, jazz | *Mood Indigo*, *Take the A Train*, *Black, Brown, and Beige* |
| **Miles Davis** | 20th century, jazz | *Kind of Blue*, *Bitches Brew*, *Sketches of Spain* |
| **Herbie Hancock** | 20th–21st century, jazz & fusion | *Head Hunters*, *Maiden Voyage*, *Future Shock* |
| **Ludwig van Beethoven** | (German) but his *Symphony No. 9* is iconic in the U.S. | *Symphony No. 9*, *Für Elise* |
| **John Cage** | 20th century, avant‑garde | *4′33″*, *Sonatas and Interludes* |
| **George Gershwin** | Early–mid‑20th century, popular & classical | *Rhapsody in Blue*, *Porgy and Bess*, *An American in Paris* |

> **Note:**  
> *“Most famous” is highly subjective and depends on context (classical, film, jazz, popular music, etc.). The table above lists a mix of composers who have had a major impact on American music history and are widely recognized both domestically and internationally.*
